cascade.comment: Ordered rule cascade for SPEC §7.1. Evaluated top to bottom; first match wins. Edge cases live here, never in engine code.

rules.explanation: Instrument type and domicile were inferred during ingestion and not confirmed by an operator. PFIC status cannot be determined from unverified metadata; a misclassification here would silently downgrade a critical flag.
sources: Meridian design decision (PHASE_REVIEW_2 S7): the cascade may only run on operator-confirmed metadata

rules.explanation: US-registered ('40 Act) fund. A domestic corporation is outside the PFIC definition.
sources: IRC s1297(a) (foreign corporation requirement)
Investment Company Act 1940

rules.explanation: Directly held security, cash or real property — not an interest in a pooled foreign corporation.
sources: IRC s1297(a)

rules.explanation: Non-US domiciled pooled vehicle held by a US person. Default treatment is the punitive excess-distribution regime: gains and 'excess' distributions are allocated across the holding period, taxed at the highest ordinary rate for prior years, plus an interest charge. QEF and mark-to-market elections exist but QEF requires a PFIC Annual Information Statement that most UK funds do not produce.
rules.filing_implication: Form 8621 required per PFIC per year (subject to the de minimis reporting exception).
sources: IRC s1291 (excess distribution regime)
IRC s1293 (QEF)
IRC s1296 (mark-to-market)
IRC s1298(f) (annual reporting)

rules.explanation: Pooled vehicle whose income and asset mix determines PFIC status under the 75%/50% tests; look-through data is not available to this system.
sources: IRC s1297(a) income and asset tests

rules.explanation: No cascade rule matched this instrument — typically a confirmed record with a missing or unrecognised domicile. The conservative reading is to refer it to the operator rather than let it fall out of the PFIC population.
sources: Meridian design decision: the cascade is total; an unmatched instrument is never treated as not-PFIC

wrapper_mitigation.comment: SPEC §7.1: a PFIC inside a treaty-recognised pension is a WARN with wrapper context, not a CRITICAL. The PFIC determination itself does not change — only the severity presented.

rules.explanation: Held inside a treaty-recognised pension wrapper. The UK/US treaty's pension articles are generally read as deferring tax on growth within the scheme, which is the usual basis for not applying PFIC reporting to holdings inside it. This is a treaty position, not a statutory exemption, and it depends on the scheme qualifying.
sources: UK/US DTA 2001 Arts. 17-18
IRC s1298(f) reporting relief is not automatic — position depends on scheme qualification

de_minimis_reference.source: Cross-reference to params/us/2026.json so thresholds stay in one place

filing_status_assumption.source: Treas. Reg. 1.1298-1(c)(2) sets a lower de minimis threshold for single filers; the ledger does not record filing status, so the lower (more filing-prone) threshold is applied

above_de_minimis.value: Aggregate PFIC value exceeds the s1298(f) de minimis reporting threshold: a Form 8621 is required for each PFIC for each year, on the excess-distribution regime unless a QEF or mark-to-market election is in place. Information only — elections and filings are not visible to this system.

below_de_minimis.value: Aggregate PFIC value is below the s1298(f) de minimis reporting threshold. The reporting exception additionally requires that no excess distribution or disposition arose in the year and that no QEF or mark-to-market election is in force — neither is visible to this system, so the exception is reported as available but unverified. The taxing regime itself is unaffected.

investable_wealth_excluded_types.source: SPEC §7.1 expresses PFIC exposure as a share of investable wealth; directly held real property is not investable wealth

situs.comment: SPEC §7.3. Ordered cascade, first match wins, evaluated per holding (instrument + the account that holds it). Situs follows the asset, not the custodian.

label.source: SPEC §7.3 requires the whole section to carry this label

attribution.source: Meridian v0 modelling assumption: a holding in a jointly owned account is attributed equally to each named owner; beneficial ownership is not recorded in the ledger

treaty_credit.value: Modelling assumption: the UK/US estate and gift tax treaty (1979) is assumed to be available, giving primary taxing rights by situs and domicile with credit relief for the other country's tax, and extending a prorated unified credit to a non-US-domiciled decedent. No treaty credit is computed here — the two columns are gross exposure, before any treaty relief.
treaty_credit.source: UK/US Estate, Gift and Generation-Skipping Tax Convention 1979, Arts. 5-9 and 11

asset_classes.comment: Every class a situs rule may assign. Classes carrying us_params_ref must appear in that list in params/us/2026.json — the module asserts it at run time.

sources: IRC s2104(a); Treas. Reg. 20.2104-1(a)(5): stock of a US corporation is US-situs wherever the certificate or custody sits, including via ADR
IRC s2104(c)
IRC s2105(b)(3) portfolio-interest debt is excluded, but the exclusion cannot be verified from a statement — the conservative reading is applied
IRC s2104; the interest in a US qualified plan or IRA is treated as US-situs property, and the plan's own holdings are not looked through
UK/US DTA 2001 Arts. 17-18 (income treatment, not situs)
IRC s2104(a) by implication: only US-corporation stock is US-situs; shares in non-US corporations, OEICs, unit trusts and non-US funds are outside US situs
IRC s2105(b)(1): deposits with a US bank not effectively connected with a US business are not US-situs
Non-US bank deposits are outside US situs entirely
IRC s2104(a): only real property situated in the US is US-situs

rules.explanation: Held inside a US retirement or education plan. The estate asset is the interest in the US plan itself, which is US-situs; the plan's underlying holdings are not looked through.

Instrument type and domicile were inferred at ingestion and not operator-confirmed. Situs cannot be assigned from unverified metadata; the value is shown separately rather than dropped into either column.
Stock of a US-incorporated issuer or fund. US-situs regardless of where it is held or in which currency it is quoted.
Debt of a US obligor. The portfolio-interest exclusion may take it out of US situs, but qualification cannot be established from a statement, so the conservative (in-scope) reading is applied.
Real property situated in the United States.
Cash deposit. Non-US deposits are outside US situs; deposits with a US bank not connected with a US trade or business are excluded by s2105(b)(1).
Security or pooled vehicle of a non-US issuer. Outside US estate tax situs, though within UK IHT scope where the owner is UK long-term resident.
Real property situated outside the United States.
No situs rule matched — typically a confirmed record with no domicile recorded. Reported separately rather than assigned to a column.

uk_iht_scope.comment: SPEC §7.3: post-2025 UK IHT scope is residence-based (params/uk/2026-27.json iht.long_term_residence_rule).

long_term_resident_flags.source: FA 2025 residence-based IHT regime: a long-term UK resident (UK-resident in 10 of the previous 20 tax years) is in scope on worldwide assets. The ledger records the operator's conclusion as uk_domicile_status; residence history is not held, so the 10-of-20 test is not recomputed here.

worldwide_note.value: Long-term UK resident: worldwide assets are within the scope of UK inheritance tax at death.
worldwide_note.source: IHTA 1984 s6 as amended by FA 2025; params/uk/2026-27.json iht.long_term_residence_rule

uk_situs_note.value: Not recorded as a long-term UK resident: UK inheritance tax is assumed to reach UK-situs assets only. Residence history is not held in the ledger, so the 10-of-20 test cannot be evaluated by this system, and the post-departure tail provisions are not modelled.
uk_situs_note.source: IHTA 1984 s6 as amended by FA 2025; Meridian v0 scope note

worldwide_note.value: US citizen or domiciliary: the worldwide estate is within the scope of US estate tax, and the situs split below is presentational only — it does not narrow the taxable estate.

us_situs_only_note.value: Not a US person: US estate tax reaches US-situs assets only, against a unified credit equivalent to a much smaller exemption than a US person receives, subject to any treaty relief.

currency_of_life.comment: SPEC §7.4. Compares the person's portfolio currency exposure with the operator-set spending currency mix.

method.value: Mismatch score is the total variation distance between the two currency distributions: half the sum of the absolute differences in share, per currency. 0.00 means the portfolio's currency split matches the spending split exactly; 1.00 means no overlap at all.
method.source: SPEC §7.4 requires a mismatch score; total variation distance is the standard bounded distance between two distributions and is symmetric and scale-free

look_through.source: Meridian v0 modelling assumption: currency exposure is taken from the quotation/valuation currency of each holding. Funds are not looked through to their underlying currency exposure, because the ledger holds no constituent data — a GBP-quoted global equity fund therefore counts as GBP exposure and the score understates true mismatch

bands.source: Meridian v0 presentation bands for the §7.4 mismatch score; presentational only, no tax consequence
